mission: Ben calls Desh and they establish the mission parameters — the reader meets Desh and feels the unspoken weight of shared GAG history between them
why_now: Ben has decided to investigate the wrongness with a partner. He's calling Desh — the choice has been made, now we see what that choice reveals about both men.
opening_hook: Desh answers like someone who's been expecting this call. Not the wrongness — just Ben needing something. Their shorthand is immediate and tells the reader these two have history.
conflict: Internal/interpersonal: Ben pitches the mission as a simple survey extension — minimizing the stakes to Desh the same way he minimized them to Luke. Desh sees through it but agrees anyway, because that's what they do.
turning_point: Desh agrees to come but drops a line that lands differently than Ben expects — a reference to their shared past that acknowledges the weight without naming it. Ben realizes Desh isn't coming as a contractor. He's coming as the friend Ben won't admit he needs.
closing_hook: Ben plots the rendezvous coordinates. The wrongness in the Force pulses — stronger now, with a directionality that wasn't there before. It's coming from somewhere specific, and his route leads straight to it.
setting: Ben's ship cockpit (holocomm to Desh's location — a private security office, functional, no personality). The contrast between their environments tells the reader about their divergent post-GAG paths.
sensory_details: Desh's dry humor cuts through holocomm static. Ben's navigation display shows the adjusted route like a thread pulled taut toward the Outer Rim. The Force wrongness is stronger — Ben can feel it even when he's not reaching for it.
emotional_trajectory: Practiced casualness -> recognition of shared weight -> quiet gratitude -> anticipation

stakes.personal: Ben's ability to ask for help without admitting he needs it
stakes.interpersonal: The Ben-Desh relationship — built on shared trauma, sustained by unspoken loyalty
stakes.external: The wrongness is getting stronger and more directional — the mission just became real

canon_elements_needed: GAG (Galactic Alliance Guard) under Jacen Solo
Ben and Desh's shared service history
notes: Desh is the non-Force-user who grounds the story. His introduction must establish him as competent and perceptive WITHOUT making him a sidekick. The GAG history is planted, not explained — PP02 pays off in Chapter 11. R01 (the wrongness has a direction) crystallizes in the closing beat.
